comparisons.peer_summary: Client operating income improved to an $897 million profit in 2024 from a $46 million operating loss in 2023, primarily due to higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose improvements in specific business segment operating incomes for 2024 compared to 2023. MU attributes CNBU operating income improvement to higher bit shipments, increased average selling prices, and cost reductions, partially offset by higher R&D expenses. AMD attributes Client segment operating income improvement to higher revenue, partially offset by higher operating expenses. While both cite revenue/shipments and cost pressures, MU explicitly details price and volume drivers for bits and R&D, whereas AMD focuses on the net revenue increase for its Client segment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD report significant operating income growth in their core high-performance computing segments (CNBU for MU, Data Center for AMD) in 2024. MU’s CNBU operating income improved due to higher bit shipments, ASP increases, and cost reductions, partially offset by higher R&D. AMD’s Data Center operating income rose from $1.3 billion to $3.5 billion, driven primarily by higher revenue (sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs), partially offset by higher R&D investment. Both companies identify higher revenue/volumes and increased R&D as key comparative factors, though AMD provides specific dollar amounts and product names while MU provides directional drivers.

Both disclosures focus on the operational drivers of segment profitability, with MU providing a more granular breakdown of volume, price, and cost factors, while NVDA attributes the growth broadly to revenue increases.
